value.overview: The Prong-billed Barbet (Semnornis frantzii) is a distinctive, fruit-eating mountain bird restricted to Costa Rica and western Panama. It has a large, heavy bill with a small hooked projection near the tip, a compact body, and contrasting dark, buff, and gray plumage. This barbet inhabits humid highland forests, especially cloud forest and forest edges rich in mosses, epiphytes, and fruiting trees. It is an important disperser of montane plant seeds.
value.classification: The Prong-billed Barbet belongs to the order Piciformes and the family Semnornithidae, a small family containing only two toucan-barbet species. Its scientific name is Semnornis frantzii, and it is generally treated as a monotypic species without recognized subspecies.
value.identification: This is a stocky, short-tailed bird with a disproportionately large, pale horn-colored bill that has a distinctive projecting tip. Adults show a dark crown and upperparts, a contrasting pale or buff face and throat, and darker lower underparts, with the exact appearance varying slightly with age and sex. The sexes are broadly similar, although males may have more developed dark feathers on the nape. Its deep, far-carrying cwa-cwa-cwa song and loud paired duets are useful for detection.
value.rangeHabitat: The Prong-billed Barbet is restricted to the mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama. In Costa Rica it occurs mainly along the Cordillera de Tilarán, the Central Volcanic Cordillera, and the Talamanca range, including both Caribbean- and Pacific-slope highlands. It is most associated with humid montane evergreen and cloud forests, generally from about 1,200 to 2,450 meters, although it can occur locally at lower elevations. It also uses forest edges, open woodland, and fruiting trees beside highland pastures.
value.migrationStatus: Resident and generally non-migratory. In Costa Rica, individuals remain in the highland mountain regions year-round, although they may make local movements in response to fruit availability. Outside the breeding season they may gather in small feeding flocks and use communal roosts.
value.breeding: Breeding usually begins in the dry season, with activity reported from about March into May in Costa Rica. Pairs are territorial and excavate nest cavities in decaying trunks, snags, or soft wood, often several meters above the ground. The usual clutch contains four or five white eggs. Both adults incubate and care for the young, and the species may occasionally receive help from other group members. Adults commonly perform duets around the nesting territory.
value.dietFeeding: The Prong-billed Barbet is primarily frugivorous. It feeds mainly in the forest canopy on a wide variety of small and medium-sized fruits, including fruits of montane trees and epiphytes. Large fruits may be torn apart, while smaller ones can be swallowed whole. Adults may also take flowers or occasional insects, and insects are especially important in the diet of nestlings. By carrying and passing seeds, the species contributes to forest regeneration.
value.behavior: This barbet is active by day and usually forages in the canopy, descending or moving to forest edges when fruit is available there. Pairs are territorial during breeding and often advertise with repeated, resonant calls or coordinated duets. Outside the breeding season, birds may form groups of up to roughly a dozen individuals and may roost communally in tree cavities. Its flight is direct and relatively rapid, and it can be unobtrusive despite its loud voice.
